promoted: {rival}, from your intake and your rival for every promotion, is promoted to {title}. The email announcing it is copied to you too, as a courtesy.
{rival} is now {title}. Your intake's group chat hears about it before you do.
{rival} makes {title}. {They} sent round a very nice message, which you have read twice.
winService: This year there was one promotion slot at your grade, and two of you up for it: you and {rival}, from your intake, your rival for every promotion. It went to you. {rival} congratulated you within the minute, so the news must have reached {them} first.
The ranking exercise could promote only one of you at this grade, and it was you. {rival} took it well, in the sense that nobody saw {them} take it.
loseService: This year there was one promotion slot at your grade, and two of you up for it: you and {rival}, from your intake, your rival for every promotion. It went to {rival}. You're told it was "very close". They tell everyone that, probably including {rival}.
The ranking exercise could promote only one of you at this grade, and it was {rival}. {senior}, your reporting officer, says you are "next in line", and doesn't say for what.
winPolitics: There was one appointment open at your level this year, and the choice was between you and {rival}. It went to you. {rival} was the first to shake your hand at the swearing-in, and held it a beat longer than necessary.
losePolitics: There was one appointment open at your level this year, and the choice was between you and {rival}. It went to {rival}. The Prime Minister's Office describes the decision as "finely balanced".
pm: {rival} is to be the next Prime Minister. {They} telephoned you before the announcement, or said {they} did.
pmBlocked: The one job above yours is taken. {rival} is Prime Minister, and shows no sign of having considered the private sector.
The one job above yours is still taken. {rival} has announced a ten-year plan, which you are choosing to read as a policy document.
elected: {rival} was introduced at a press conference as a new candidate, and won. Your batchmate is now a Member of Parliament.
lostSeat: {rival} stood for Parliament and lost the ward. A month later {rival} was back in the service at the same grade, which everyone agreed to call a homecoming.
consultancy: {rival} is leaving the service for the private sector. The farewell lunch is at a hotel, so the new package must be very good.
scandal: {rival} has resigned, for personal reasons. Everyone has a theory. Nobody says it in the lift.
rankedBelowService: The ranking exercise put {rival}, from your intake and your rival for every promotion, above you this year. Neither of you went up: the slot went to someone from another division whom you have never met.
You were ranked just below {rival} this year, and neither of you was promoted. It is the one comparison everyone on the floor made, and nobody made out loud.
rankedBelowPolitics: When the appointments were settled, {rival}'s name was ahead of yours on the list. Neither of you moved. Someone from the back bench did.
appointed: {rival} is appointed {title}. The swearing-in photograph is on the front page, and you are in the background of it.
{rival} is now {title}. Your intake's group chat hears about it before you do.
promotedApart: {rival} is now {title}. You hear about it at a dinner, from someone who assumes you already knew.
{rival} is now {title}. Your intake's group chat hears about it before you do.
electedTogether: {rival} stood at the same general election, in another constituency, and won. Your batchmate is now a Member of Parliament too.
lostSeatTogether: {rival} stood at the same general election, in another constituency, and lost. A month later {rival} was back in the service at the same grade, which everyone agreed to call a homecoming.
consultancyPolitics: {rival} has left Parliament for a seat on a company's board. The papers call it "an orderly transition". They call all of them that.
scandalPolitics: {rival} has resigned from Parliament, for personal reasons. Everyone has a theory. Nobody says it in the lobby.
retired: {rival} retires as {title}. There is a farewell lunch. You send a card, and mean it.

folder.item: a peer assessment of {rival} that did you more good than it did {them}

events.title: The 360
events.body: It's 360-degree feedback season, when colleagues assess each other anonymously and the ranking panel reads the results. You've been asked to assess {rival}, from your intake, who is your rival for every promotion. The form promises anonymity. It has a free-text box headed "Areas for development".

choices.outcome: Three sentences on stakeholder management, true and mildly painful. {rival} acts on all three within a year and never learns where they came from.
It is accurate. It is also the only peer comment the ranking panel quotes. {rival} is described that year as "still developing", which you did not write but did cause.
The form accepts it. HR's report later notes "limited peer input" for your whole division: the only comment that year that is about you.

events.title: Annex B
events.body: {rival}, from your intake and your rival for every promotion, sends a paper up to the Permanent Secretary at nine tomorrow, and you're copied on the draft. Annex B has the right numbers in the wrong columns, and the recommendation rests on them. A mistake like that would cost {rival} at the next ranking.

choices.outcome: {rival} fixes it at 11:50pm and says thank you twice, the second time in a voice you have not heard before.

choices.text: Say nothing. It is not your paper.
choices.outcome: The Permanent Secretary finds Annex B in four minutes. For the rest of the year {rival} is described as "detail-light". You are described as nothing at all, which this year is better.

choices.text: Raise it at the meeting, helpfully.
choices.outcome: You are thanked for your rigour. {rival} thanks you too, later, in the corridor, in a tone the minutes would not have captured.

events.title: One Posting
events.body: There's one two-year posting to the Budget Division at the Ministry of Finance this year, the kind that gets people noticed, and your division has two nominees: you and {rival}, from your intake. HR suggests the two of you "have a conversation" first. In HR, that means one of you should withdraw.

choices.text: Withdraw, and say it was your idea.
choices.outcome: {rival} goes to Finance. Three weeks later a photograph arrives of the view from {their} new office. It is, admittedly, a very good view.

choices.text: Let HR decide on the files.

contest.winText: The posting goes to you. {rival} says {they} had expected it to, which may even be true.
contest.loseText: The posting goes to {rival}. HR's email to you uses the phrase "many strong candidates". There were two.

choices.outcome: HR decides on the files, which takes six weeks and a matrix.

choices.text: Make your case to the Director, privately.

contest.winText: The posting goes to you. {rival} hears, eventually, how.
contest.loseText: The posting goes to {rival}. The Director mentions, in passing, that {rival} did not come to see her about it.

choices.outcome: The Director listens, nods, and says she will "bear it in mind". That is the most anyone has ever got from her.

events.title: Views Are Sought
events.body: {rival}, from your intake, has been shortlisted for a post one grade above you both, which would make {rival} senior to you. The selection panel has asked {rival}'s peers for their views. Yours will be read, and filed, and remembered by someone.

choices.outcome: You write half a page and mean all of it. Someone on the panel later shows it to {rival}, who never mentions it to you and never forgets it.
Two lines, both true, neither memorable. The panel files them with the others.

choices.text: Suggest, carefully, that another year at grade might help {them}.
choices.outcome: The panel finds your view "balanced". {rival} learns of it eventually, the way everyone here learns everything: from someone who was not supposed to say.

events.title: Saturday
events.body: {rival}, your batchmate, is an MP too, and {rival}'s ward has had a difficult year: a lift upgrading that overran, and a letter in the Forum page every week. {They} asked you to walk the ward with {them} on Saturday morning. Your own ward has a walkabout planned for the same morning.

choices.outcome: Six blocks, two markets, and one auntie who assumes you are {rival}'s campaign manager and tells you exactly what she thinks of {them}. The letters to the Forum stop by March.
Your volunteers are better at it than you are. {rival} thanks them by name, which you notice.
Your ward is pleased to see you. {rival} manages without you, and remembers the Saturday.

events.title: First Among Equals
events.body: Who becomes the next Prime Minister, first among equals, is being settled informally by the Cabinet, in a room. It has come down to two names, as your intake joked it would at its first dinner: yours and {rival}'s.

choices.outcome: You say it plainly, to the people who need to hear it. {rival} says it too, in the next room. It will be decided the way these things are: slowly, and then all at once.
{rival} thanks you once, in private, and never again. That is how you know it was understood.

events.title: The Name Put Forward
events.body: {rival}, your batchmate and now senior to you, has been asked to nominate officers for a cross-ministry task force. Everyone understands it is where future leaders get tested. {They} put your name first.

choices.outcome: Lunch, on you, at a place {rival} chose. It was more expensive than {they} let on, and worth it.

choices.text: Decline. You would rather go up on your own file.
choices.outcome: {rival} says that is fair. It is, and it costs you a year.
